segments.text: Thanks for making the time today, Rachel and Dev. My goal is to understand how your team runs customer calls today and whether Fanthom is a fit.
Happy to. Quick context: we run about forty carrier and shipper calls a week across the operations team, and nobody takes consistent notes.
The biggest problem is that follow-ups fall through the cracks. A shipper asks for a rate change, and two weeks later nobody remembers who owned it.
How are you capturing notes right now? Is it a shared doc, the CRM, something else?
Mostly a shared Google Doc per account, plus whatever people remember to paste into HubSpot. Honestly it's pretty manual and it's slow.
I spend maybe three hours a week just cleaning up call notes before our Monday pipeline review.
That's really common. What would good look like for you six months from now?
Every call has a summary and action items in HubSpot within five minutes, and I can search across calls when a customer escalates.
Got it. And who else would be involved in evaluating a tool like this?
I own the budget for ops tooling, but our security team has to sign off, and Dev will run the pilot.
Security will want to see your SOC 2 report and data retention settings before anything touches customer calls.
Totally fair. I can send the SOC 2 report and our DPA today after this call.
What does pricing look like for a team of about twenty five people?
For twenty five seats on the Team plan you'd be around nineteen dollars per seat per month, billed annually, with volume discounts above fifty seats.
That's within what we budgeted for this quarter. My concern is adoption. We tried a notes tool last year and people stopped using it after a month.
That's the right concern. Fanthom joins automatically from the calendar, so nobody has to remember to start it. Most teams see ninety percent coverage in week one.
Can we run a pilot with the dispatch team first? Maybe ten people for two weeks.
Yes, let's do that. I'll set up a two week pilot for ten seats starting next Monday, and I'll schedule a check-in at the end of week one.
Great. We decided to target a go or no-go decision by the end of the month, so that timeline works.
I'll send over the list of pilot users and our HubSpot admin contact by Friday.
Perfect. Thanks both, I'll follow up with the security docs and the pilot plan this afternoon.
